question_text:
Compute the density for iron at $700^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, given that its room-temperature density is $7.870 \mathrm{~g} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$. Assume that the volume coefficient of thermal expansion, $a{v}$, is equal to $3 a{I}$.

Reference:
"Table 17.1 Thermal Properties for a Variety of Materials
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|l|}
\hline Material & $\left(\begin{array}{c}c_p \\ (J / k g \cdot K)\end{array}{ }^a\right.$ & $\left[\left({ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\right)^{-1} \times 10^{\alpha_1} \times 10^{-6}\right]^b$ & $\boldsymbol{k}$ $(\mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m} \cdot \mathrm{K})^c$ & L $\left[\Omega \cdot W /(K)^2 \times 10^{-8}\right]$ \\
\hline \multicolumn{5}{|c|}{Metals} \\
\hline Aluminum & 900 & 23.6 & 247 & 2.20 \\
\hline Copper & 386 & 17.0 & 398 & 2.25 \\
\hline Gold & 128 & 14.2 & 315 & 2.50 \\
\hline Iron & 448 & 11.8 & 80 & 2.71 \\
\hline Nickel & 443 & 13.3 & 90 & 2.08 \\
\hline Silver & 235 & 19.7 & 428 & 2.13 \\
\hline Tungsten & 138 & 4.5 & 178 & 3.20 \\
\hline 1025 Steel & 486 & 12.0 & 51.9 & - \\
\hline 316 Stainless steel & 502 & 16.0 & 15.9 & - \\
\hline Brass (70Cu-30Zn) & 375 & 20.0 & 120 & - \\
\hline Kovar (54Fe-29Ni-17Co) & 460 & 5.1 & 17 & 2.80 \\
\hline Invar ( $64 \mathrm{Fe}-36 \mathrm{Ni}$ ) & 500 & 1.6 & 10 & 2.75 \\
\hline Super Invar (63Fe-32Ni-5Co) & 500 & 0.72 & 10 & 2.68 \\
\hline \multicolumn{5}{|c|}{Ceramics} \\
\hline Alumina ( $\mathrm{Al}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$ ) & 775 & 7.6 & 39 & - \\
\hline Magnesia (MgO) & 940 & $13.5{ }^{\text {d }}$ & 37.7 & - \\
\hline Spinel ( $\mathrm{MgAl}_2 \mathrm{O}_4$ ) & 790 & $7.6{ }^{\text {d }}$ & $15.0{ }^{\text {e }}$ & - \\
\hline Fused silica ( $\mathrm{SiO}_2$ ) & 740 & 0.4 & 1.4 & - \\
\hline Soda-lime glass & 840 & 9.0 & 1.7 & - \\
\hline Borosilicate (Pyrex) glass & 850 & 3.3 & 1.4 & - \\
\hline \multicolumn{5}{|c|}{Polymers} \\
\hline Polyethylene (high density) & 1850 & 106-198 & 0.46-0.50 & - \\
\hline Polypropylene & 1925 & 145-180 & 0.12 & - \\
\hline Polystyrene & 1170 & 90-150 & 0.13 & - \\
\hline Polytetrafluoroethylene (Teflon) & 1050 & 126-216 & 0.25 & - \\
\hline Phenol-formaldehyde, phenolic & 1590-1760 & 122 & 0.15 & - \\
\hline Nylon 6,6 & 1670 & 144 & 0.24 & - \\

\end{tabular}
${ }^a$ To convert to $\mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{g} \cdot \mathrm{K}$, multiply by $2.39 \times 10^{-4}$; to convert to $\mathrm{Btu} / \mathrm{lb}_{\mathrm{m}} \cdot{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{F}$, multiply by $2.39 \times 10^{-4}$.
${ }^b$ To convert to $\left({ }^{\circ} \mathrm{F}\right)^{-1}$, multiply by 0.56 .
${ }^{\circ}$ To convert to $\mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{s} \cdot \mathrm{cm} \cdot \mathrm{K}$, multiply by $2.39 \times 10^{-3}$; to convert to $\mathrm{Btu} / \mathrm{ft} \cdot \mathrm{h} \cdot{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{F}$, multiply by 0.578 .
${ }^d$ Value measured at $100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$.
${ }^{\circ}$ Mean value taken over the temperature range $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $1000^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$."The unit of the answer is g/cm^3.
response:
## Solution

The density at elevated temperature accounts for thermal volume expansion:

$$\rho(T) = \frac{\rho_0}{1 + \alpha_v \Delta T}$$

**Given values:**
- Room-temperature density: $\rho_0 = 7.870\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$
- Linear expansion coefficient (from Table 17.1, Iron): $\alpha_l = 11.8 \times 10^{-6}\ (^{\circ}\mathrm{C})^{-1}$
- Volume expansion coefficient: $\alpha_v = 3\alpha_l = 3(11.8\times10^{-6}) = 35.4\times10^{-6}\ (^{\circ}\mathrm{C})^{-1}$
- Temperature change (taking room temperature as $20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$): $\Delta T = 700 - 20 = 680^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$

**Calculation:**

$$\alpha_v \Delta T = (35.4\times10^{-6})(680) = 0.024072$$

$$\rho(700^{\circ}\mathrm{C}) = \frac{7.870}{1 + 0.024072} = \frac{7.870}{1.024072} \approx 7.685\ \mathrm{g/cm^3}$$

$$\boxed{7.685}$$
